key_insight: SILSA replaces fragmented voxel-based 3D generation with compact sliding-window slice latents, helping preserve topology while reducing generation cost. The core idea is to keep surfaces more continuous so thin and highly connected structures are represented more faithfully.
problem_solved: Existing high-resolution 3D generation methods often split shapes into many local tokens, which makes generation expensive and can break topological consistency, especially for thin structures or complex connections.
method: Represents 3D shapes using compact sliding-window slice latents instead of dense voxel token pipelines.
Generates local geometry in a topology-aware way while maintaining continuity across neighboring slices.
Reduces token fragmentation and improves efficiency compared with multi-stage active-structure-then-geometry workflows.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, SILSA offers a more efficient path to high-resolution 3D generation with better shape integrity. This is especially useful for applications where topology matters, such as CAD, robotics, and digital content creation.

paper_title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
paper_authors: Tianjiao Yu, Xinzhuo Li, Yifan Shen, Ying Shen, Kiet A. Nguyen
